lesson_basics_lenses_continue: Open the lens interface by clicking any of the lens buttons
lesson_basics_lenses_complete_desc: Each Lens has its own map mode! Zoom out and take a look at the map to see what details just changed. Clicking on each lens and looking at the map can give you a good hunch of what's currently going on in your country.\n\nWhen you're ready to move on, close the lens and press Next.
lesson_basics_lenses_complete_continue: Close the lens interface by clicking the lens button again
lesson_pops_intro_desc:
Pops are a way to split up a country's population into convenient groupings of people of the same [concept_profession], [Concept('concept_building','Workplace')] in a [concept_state], [concept_culture], and [concept_religion] - in other words, a distinct demographic of people who share an economic and political role in society.

In this lesson we will first look at a #b Summary#! of Pops in your country, and then look at the #b Details#! of a particular Pop.

To get started, click the highlighted 'Population' icon.
lesson_pops_summary_desc: Here you can see a high-level summary of what kinds of Pops live in your country and what their share of the [concept_political_strength] is. But we want more details, so click on the highlighted 'Detailed List' to see a list of all individual Pops in [GetPlayer.GetName].
lesson_pops_country_details_desc:
This list of [Concept('concept_profession', '$concept_professions$')] display:
$TAB$total #v number#! of individuals
$TAB$total [concept_political_strength]
$TAB$which [Concept('concept_interest_group', '$concept_interest_groups$')] are dominant among them
$TAB$average [concept_sol]

We can get a similar view for a particular state from the State Overview Panel. Click on any of your states now and go to the Overview tab.
lesson_pops_country_details_continue: Click on any of your states and open the Overview tab
lesson_pops_state_population_desc: The State Overview panel provides only some basic population statistics. Access the Population details for this particular state by clicking the highlighted tab.
lesson_pops_state_population_back: State Overview tab is #b not#! open
lesson_pops_state_population_details_des: This is a similar view to the previous one, but this time only for the Pops in the state you're looking at rather than everyone in your country. Similar views are available throughout the game to aggregate and categorize information about your Pops.\n\nLet's go deeper by clicking on one of these categories to show a list of all Pops of that Profession. These individual Pops are also clickable to show the most fine-grained details available on that particular demographic.
lesson_pops_state_population_details_con: Expand a pop list, then click on an individual Pop
lesson_pops_stats_1_desc: Here we see an individual Pop in all its glory. While you never interact directly with a Pop, every action you take affects the properties of Pops in your country. Your country changes in turn as the capabilities, conditions, mobility, and desires of your population changes.\n\nWe will now go over the properties of a Pop. While running your country you will almost always deal with these values as averages or aggregates, but sometimes it's necessary to drill down to the individual level to see #b why#! a value is what it is. For every value there is always an explanatory tooltip available.
lesson_pops_stats_1_back: Individual Pop tab is #b not#! open
lesson_pops_stats_2_desc:
A Pop's [concept_profession] determines what job the Pop's [concept_workforce] does for a living, which influences their [concept_building_wage] and what [Concept('concept_interest_group', '$concept_interest_groups$')] they might support. Each Profession is considered part of the [Concept('concept_lower_strata','Lower')], [Concept('concept_middle_strata','Middle')], or [Concept('concept_upper_strata','Upper Strata')], which can affect their [Concept('concept_taxes','$concept_tax_rate$')] among other things.

A Pop does not switch Profession all at once. When job openings are created in a [concept_building] in the same [concept_state], Pops who [Concept('concept_pop_qualifications','qualify')] for the new job will be offered a certain number of them. If the new job is better than their current one, some individuals in the [concept_workforce] will take their [concept_dependents] and join an existing Pop of the suitable Profession, or create a new one if one does not already exist.

All this happens without your interference, and you will rarely be aware of it other than when new positions aren't filled in a reasonable amount of time. Over time you will notice how demographics shift along with the Professions offered in your country.
lesson_pops_stats_3_desc: A Pop's [concept_sol] is a combination of their [concept_wealth] and the conditions where they live. It determines their general satisfaction with their situation and influences their [Concept('concept_pop_growth','Growth')].\n\nAs Standard of Living increases, a number of individuals in the Pop will become [Concept('concept_loyalist', '$concept_loyalists$')]. When it decreases the Pop will become more [concept_radical], and for as long as it remains below an expected national minimum more and more of them will turn into [Concept('concept_radical', '$concept_radicals$')].
lesson_pops_stats_4_desc: This section lists in which [concept_state] the [concept_pop] lives and works, its [concept_literacy] rate, and its [concept_culture] and [concept_religion].\n\nThese aspects are particularly important for determining a $concept_pop$'s employability. $concept_pops$ can only take jobs available in the [concept_state] where they live. $concept_pops$ with a low [concept_acceptance_status] have a harder time [Concept('concept_pop_qualifications','qualifying')] for better [Concept('concept_profession', '$concept_professions$')], and a high [concept_literacy] rate is crucial for qualifying for those more technical or academic jobs that emerge with modernity.
lesson_pops_stats_5_desc: This section lists various values about this [concept_pop], among them its size, their [concept_social_class], [Concept('concept_interest_group', '$concept_interest_groups$')] the Pop supports, how much [concept_political_strength] it can support them with, and how many of its members are currently [Concept('concept_radical', '$concept_radicals$')] and [Concept('concept_loyalist', '$concept_loyalists$')].\n\nInterest Groups favor different [Concept('concept_law', '$concept_laws$')] depending on their [Concept('concept_ideology', '$concept_ideologies$')], and will use the Political Strength lent to them by Pops to pursue these policies. Loyalists and Radicals both contribute to the [concept_approval] of the Interest Groups the Pop supports. Radicals also create [concept_turmoil] in the Pop's [concept_state].
lesson_pops_stats_5_continue: Open Economy tab in Individual Pop panel
lesson_pops_stats_6_desc: A single Pop consists of both [concept_workforce] and [concept_dependents]. The former works the country's [Concept('concept_building', '$concept_buildings$')] in exchange for a [concept_building_wage]. The latter are either unable to work on account of age or injuries, or oversee a household, rear children, take care of the elderly, or perform odd jobs. Usually both Workforce and Dependents contribute to a Pop's total income, but wages represent the lion's share.\n\nBoth Workforce and Dependents have [concept_pop_needs] that must be met, and will spend their income on [Concept('concept_good', '$concept_goods$')] to satisfy them. If there is money left over the Pop's [concept_wealth] will build up over time. If income is insufficient to cover expenses, Wealth will be drained.
lesson_pops_stats_6_back: Economy tab in Individual Pop panel is #b not#! open
lesson_pops_conclusion_desc: Pops are the building blocks of your country, and managing your Pops is key to successful society building. Creating jobs and enacting policies to make your Pops wealthier, happier, and more literate will provide many benefits but also new challenges. The changes you make impact your Pops who in turn will be more or less inclined to accept future changes.
lesson_expand_building_how_1_desc: [Concept('concept_building', '$concept_buildings$')] are built in [Concept('concept_state', '$concept_states$')]. By clicking a $concept_state$ on the map you can see which $concept_buildings$ already exist there, or can be built there.\n\nFind the $concept_state$ called [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetState.GetName] on the map. If you hover the $concept_state$'s name with your cursor, it should highlight somewhere in [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetState.GetCountry.GetName].
lesson_expand_building_how_1_continue: Click on the $concept_state$ of [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetState.GetName] on the map
lesson_expand_building_how_2_desc: You can find all [Concept('concept_building','$concept_buildings$')] in [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetState.GetName] under the $concept_buildings$ tab.
lesson_expand_building_how_3_desc: In the Building Overview panel you will see an overview of [Concept('concept_building', '$concept_buildings$')] that are present in the [concept_state] of [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetState.GetName], grouped by the four categories #b Urban#!, #b Resource#!, #b Agriculture#!, and #b Development#!.
lesson_expand_building_how_3_continue: Click on the [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetName] in the $concept_state$ Panel
lesson_expand_building_how_4_desc:
You can now see detailed information about the [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetName] [concept_building] in [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetState.GetName]. You can order its expansion from the panel by clicking the highlighted '+' button.

You can also use the lenses to expand the [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetName], but we will cover that later.

Begin the expansion of the [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetName] in [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetState.GetName].
lesson_expand_building_how_5_desc:
You have successfully ordered the expansion of the [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetName] in [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetState.GetName]!

[Concept('concept_building', '$concept_buildings$')] take time to expand. The [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetName] have been placed in the [concept_construction_queue] and will be constructed within several weeks.

While waiting for this process to complete, keep playing the game! More [Concept('concept_journal_entry', '$concept_journal_entries$')] will appear to teach you about the different game mechanics in Victoria 3.
lesson_expand_building_why_1K_desc: A safe way of growing your economy is by expanding a basic resource [concept_building] that produces a staple [concept_good] like [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetBuildingTarget.GetDefaultOutputGoods.GetName].\n\nStaples are [Concept('concept_good_consumption','$concept_good_consumed$')] directly by most of your [Concept('concept_pop','$concept_pops$')], who will buy it from the producing [concept_building]. This enriches its [concept_workforce], who you can [Concept('concept_taxes','$concept_tax$')] to earn [concept_money] for the [concept_treasury]. These funds can be used to expand other parts of your industry.
lesson_expand_building_why_1K_original_d: Expanding a [concept_building] is one of the best ways for you to grow your economy. It generally means that you enrich your [Concept('concept_pop', '$concept_pops$')] who you then tax and get your income from. Richer $concept_pops$ means more wealth for you to tax.\n\nLet us use your [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetName] in [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetState.GetName] as an example. If you hover the name of [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetState.GetName] the [concept_state] should highlight somewhere on the map of [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetState.GetCountry.GetName].
lesson_expand_building_why_1K_p2_desc: We will use your [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetName] in [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetState.GetName] as an example. Hover your mouse over the [concept_state] name: [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetState.GetName]. This will highlight its location somewhere on the map of [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetState.GetCountry.GetName].
lesson_expand_building_why_1_continue: Click on the $concept_state$ of [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetState.GetName] on the map
lesson_expand_building_why_2_desc: All [Concept('concept_building', '$concept_buildings$')] in [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetState.GetName] can be found under the $concept_buildings$ tab.
lesson_expand_building_why_2_back: $concept_state$ panel must be closed to backtrack
lesson_expand_building_why_3_desc: In the [concept_building] Overview panel you will see an overview of $concept_buildings$ that are present in the [concept_state] of [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetState.GetName], grouped by the four categories #b Urban#!, #b Resource#!, #b Agriculture#!, and #b Development#!.
lesson_expand_building_why_3_continue: Click on the [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetName] in the $concept_state$ Panel
lesson_expand_building_why_3_back: $concept_buildings$ panel must be closed to backtrack
lesson_expand_building_why_4_desc: Under the #v Process#! section we find the [Concept('concept_building','$concept_building_possessive$')] #v Weekly [concept_building_balance]#!. A positive $concept_building_balance$ means the $concept_building$ is profitable, and you can see how that profit is allocated in the tooltip.\n\nIf an $concept_building_industry$ has a negative #v Weekly $concept_building_balance$#! it loses money, which is generally bad. This will be covered in an upcoming Tutorial challenge.
lesson_expand_building_why_4_back: The [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetName]'s #b Information#! panel must be closed to backtrack
lesson_expand_building_why_5_desc: These are the [Concept('concept_building', '$concept_building_possessive$')] Expenses. Expenses always includes the [Concept('concept_building_wage','$concept_building_wages$')] of the $concept_building$'s [concept_workforce]. It may also include other Expenses, in @money![concept_money] or other currencies, such as [Concept('concept_good', '$concept_goods$')] required in the manufacturing process or [concept_infrastructure_usage] levied on its [concept_state].
lesson_expand_building_why_6k1_desc: These are the [Concept('concept_building', '$concept_building_possessive$')] Revenues.\n\n[GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetName] produce [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetBuildingTarget.GetDefaultOutputGoods.GetTextIcon][Nbsp][GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetBuildingTarget.GetDefaultOutputGoods.GetName] as their primary output [concept_good], but may also have secondary products. Many [Concept('concept_building', '$concept_buildings$')] can produce several different types of $concept_goods$.
lesson_expand_building_why_6k2_desc: Produced $concept_goods$ are sold, to [Concept('concept_pop','$concept_pops$')] or other $concept_buildings$, at prices that fluctuate depending on [concept_market] conditions.
lesson_expand_building_why_7_desc: [Concept('concept_building', '$concept_buildings$')] do not provide its income to you directly, but provide your [Concept('concept_pop', '$concept_pops$')] with [Concept('concept_profession','$concept_profession_jobs$')] and [Concept('concept_building_wage','$concept_building_wages$')]. You can see which $concept_pops$ work here under the #v Workforce#! tab.
lesson_expand_building_why_7_continue: Click the Workforce tab in the [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetName] Panel
lesson_expand_building_why_8_desc: One way for you to gain income from this is to tax the employed [Concept('concept_pop', '$concept_pops$')]. How much you tax is up to you and can be changed on the Budget panel.
lesson_expand_building_why_8_back: Workforce tab in the [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetName] panel must be closed to backtrack
lesson_expand_building_why_9k_desc: Expanding a [concept_building] such as [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetName] increases how many [Concept('concept_pop', '$concept_pops$')] can work there, and enriches the rest of your [Concept('concept_country','$concept_country_possessive$')] $concept_pops$ by giving them access to [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetBuildingTarget.GetDefaultOutputGoods.GetTextIcon][Nbsp][GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetBuildingTarget.GetDefaultOutputGoods.GetName] at a lower cost than before.
lesson_expand_building_why_10_desc: But before you go and expand all your [Concept('concept_building', '$concept_buildings$')], remember that there is a #v cost#! to expanding $concept_buildings$ and not all $concept_buildings$ are suitable for expansion.\n\nYou will learn more about how to identify good candidates for expansion in upcoming tutorial challenges. For now, expanding Agricultural $concept_buildings$ such as [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetName] are usually a safe bet.
lesson_expand_basic_building_started_1_d:
You have successfully ordered the expansion of the [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetName] in [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetState.GetName]!

[Concept('concept_building', '$concept_buildings$')] take time to expand. The [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetName] have been placed in the [concept_construction_queue] of [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetState.GetName] and will be assembled over time by the [concept_workforce] of the [Concept('concept_state', '$concept_state_possessive$')] [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetState.GetBuilding('building_construction_sector').GetName].

While waiting for this process to complete, keep playing the game! More [Concept('concept_journal_entry', '$concept_journal_entries$')] will appear to teach you about the different game mechanics in Victoria 3.
lesson_expand_basic_building_complete_de: The expansion of the [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetName] in [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetState.GetName] you ordered some time ago is now complete! The [concept_building] can now support a larger [concept_workforce] and produce more [Concept('concept_good', '$concept_goods$')]. You also will no longer have to pay weekly material costs for the $concept_goods$ required in its expansion.\n\nThe rate by which you can order the expansion of $concept_buildings$ across [GetPlayer.GetNameNoFlag] is limited by your [GetBuildingType('building_construction_sector').GetName], which can be expanded in exactly the same way as $concept_building_industries$! Having [GetBuildingType('building_construction_sector').GetName] $concept_buildings$ in the same [concept_state] as the $concept_buildings$ under construction will increase [concept_construction] efficiency.
lesson_expand_productive_building_how_1_: By this point you already know that you can expand [Concept('concept_building', '$concept_buildings$')] by going through the [concept_state] panel, selecting the $concept_building$, and pressing the + button or use the Production lens. You can complete this [concept_journal_entry] the same way if you like.\n\nBut for our current purposes, a better way is to go through the $concept_buildings$ overview panel to find and expand a particularly [Concept('concept_productivity', '$concept_productive$')] $concept_building$.
lesson_expand_productive_building_how_2_: Here all [Concept('concept_building', '$concept_buildings$')] across all of [GetPlayer.GetName] are displayed in a convenient list view. You can access the $concept_buildings$ directly from the list and perform common operations such as expanding, [Concept('concept_subsidies', '$concept_subsidizing$')], or changing its [Concept('concept_production_method', '$concept_production_methods$')]. More importantly, from this panel you can perform these operations on all $concept_buildings$ of a certain type in your country at once!\n\nThe [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetBuildingType.GetName] we want to build up is under the #v [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetBuildingType.GetTabName]#! tab.
Locate the $concept_building$ by expanding the #v [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetBuildingType.GetName]#! drop-down menu.

Expand the [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetBuildingType.GetName] drop-down menu in the [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetBuildingType.GetTabName] tab to locate the [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetName] in [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetState.GetName]
$concept_buildings$ panel must be closed to backtrack
lesson_expand_productive_building_how_3_: One of the most important aspects of a [concept_building] is its [concept_productivity]. The high $concept_productivity$ of the [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetName] in [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetState.GetName] is what led us to select it for expansion. $concept_productivity$ is a better measurement than profit to determine how valuable a $concept_building$ is to you, since it measures the value it adds to your economy without considering aspects like [Concept('concept_building_wage', '$concept_building_wages$')], [concept_taxes], [concept_subsidies], and [concept_dividends] which can vary drastically from building to building.
Close the [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetBuildingType.GetName] drop-down menu in the [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetBuildingType.GetTabName] tab to backtrack
lesson_expand_productive_building_how_4_: Now let’s start expansion of this building. Either click the + button as before, or *right-click* and select the appropriate option.
lesson_expand_productive_building_how_5_: Great job! Now continue to explore the game while you wait for the expansion to finish. You could go check out more in depth #v Why#! you should expand [Concept('concept_productivity', '$concept_productive$')] [Concept('concept_building', '$concept_buildings$')] by going back to the #v Tell me why#!-button in the [concept_journal_entry].
Stop expansion of the [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetName] to backtrack
lesson_expand_productive_building_why_1_: By focusing your expansion efforts on highly [Concept('concept_productivity', '$concept_productive$')] [Concept('concept_building', '$concept_buildings$')] you maximize the amount of value your [concept_workforce] adds to your economy. Producing low-value [Concept('concept_good', '$concept_goods$')] like [GetGoods('grain').GetTextIcon][Nbsp][GetGoods('grain').GetName] while spending only a small amount of [concept_money] on input $concept_goods$ like [GetGoods('tools').GetTextIcon][Nbsp][GetGoods('tools').GetName] lets your [Concept('concept_pop', '$concept_population$')] feed themselves while earning meager [Concept('concept_building_wage', '$concept_building_wages$')]. By redirecting that $concept_workforce$ to production of high-value $concept_goods$ like [GetGoods('wine').GetTextIcon][Nbsp][GetGoods('wine').GetName] or [GetGoods('clippers').GetTextIcon][Nbsp][GetGoods('clippers').GetName] instead, as long as demand is there, those $concept_pops$ will end up generating more $concept_money$ overall—even though their own $concept_building_wages$ may remain the same.
Open the $concept_building$ details panel for the [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetName] in [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetState.GetName]
lesson_expand_productive_building_why_2_: Relative [concept_productivity] is indicated by the gear icon [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetProfitabilityCompareIconInType]. Hover it for more details.
lesson_expand_productive_building_why_3_: [concept_productivity] is based only on the difference between the cost of input [Concept('concept_good', '$concept_goods$')] and the revenue earned by sales of output $concept_goods$, divided across the total [concept_workforce] of the [concept_building]. You can think of it as
lesson_expand_productive_building_why_4_: Even if the [concept_productivity] value is much higher than the Average [Concept('concept_building_wage', '$concept_building_wages$')] the difference is not wasted. It is split between the $concept_building$'s [concept_cash_reserves] and [concept_dividends] paid out to the [concept_building_owners]. Conversely, if the $concept_productivity$ is insufficient to pay the $concept_building$'s requisite $concept_building_wages$ the difference will be subtracted from the $concept_cash_reserves$ in the short-term before reducing $concept_building_wages$ and potentially [concept_throughput] in the long-term.
lesson_expand_productive_building_why_5_: Adding value to your economy by expanding only highly [Concept('concept_productivity', '$concept_productive$')] [Concept('concept_building', '$concept_buildings$')] might not be the wisest course of action in all circumstances. Oversaturating a [concept_market] will decrease the [concept_market_price] for the produced [Concept('concept_good', '$concept_goods$')] and put a lot of demand strain on the consumed $concept_goods$, leading to a decrease in $concept_productivity$ over time.
lesson_journal_1_desc_short: You have just been given your first tutorial challenge! We have #v paused the game#! to give you time to read. Remember to #v unpause#! using the speed controls or the #v Spacebar#! when you're ready to resume.\n\n#v Open the journal#! by clicking the highlighted button on the left to begin.
lesson_journal_1_desc:
You have just been given your first tutorial challenge! All tutorial challenges you receive take the form of entries in your [Concept('concept_journal_entry','$concept_journal$')]. You can complete them at your own pace with as much or as little guidance as you feel you need.

We have now #v paused the game#! again to give you time to read, and will continue to do so as we start new lessons. Remember to #v unpause#! using the speed controls or the #v Spacebar#! when you're ready to resume.

#v Open the journal#! by clicking the highlighted button on the left to begin.
lesson_journal_1_continue: Open the Journal panel by clicking the highlighted button
lesson_journal_2_desc: This is your journal. All tutorial challenges granted to you can be found here. Other major events in your country may also appear here from time to time.\n\nYou should inspect the tutorial challenge you have been given. Open the #v $je_tutorial_expand_basic_building$#! [concept_journal_entry] to continue.
lesson_journal_2_back: Journal panel must be closed to backtrack
lesson_journal_3_desc_short:
You have been tasked with expanding a basic agricultural [concept_building] in one of your [Concept('concept_state', '$concept_states$')]. As you play the game, more tutorial challenges like this one will appear in your [Concept('concept_journal_entry','$concept_journal$')].

You can either try to complete the challenge yourself without any guidance or click the #v Tell Me How#! button for a walkthrough. You can also click the #v Tell Me Why#! button for a more in-depth explanation of why it is important.

Good luck!
lesson_journal_3_desc:
You have been tasked with expanding a basic agricultural [concept_building] in one of your [Concept('concept_state', '$concept_states$')].

By completing tutorial challenges you will learn both #b how#! and #b why#! to shape your nation in the direction you desire. You can try to complete these tasks using only the information provided in the [concept_journal_entry] or you can click the 'Guide Me' button in the $concept_journal_entry$ to give you step-by-step instructions.

Additional tutorial challenges will be granted to you as you progress. Check your Journal from time to time for next steps!
lesson_journal_3_back: [concept_journal_entry] panel must be closed to backtrack
lesson_budget_balance_1_desc: You are currently spending more money on fixed expenses than you are bringing in, resulting in a budget deficit that will drain your [concept_gold_reserves] if you have any and increase the [concept_loans] if you do not. To begin resolving this problem, first bring up the Budget panel.
lesson_budget_balance_2_desc: Here you can see a breakdown of all expenses and sources of revenue and adjust tax and government wage levels. The simplest way to resolve a budget deficit is usually to increase the level at which you are taxing your [Concept('concept_pop', '$concept_pops$')] or introduce a new [Concept('concept_consumption_tax', '$concept_consumption_taxes$')], but be aware that this has drawbacks in the form of lowered [concept_wealth] and potential [concept_turmoil]. You could also try reducing your expenses by reducing the levels of your [Concept('concept_government_building', '$concept_government_buildings$')] such as [GetBuildingType('building_barrack').GetName] and [GetBuildingType('building_naval_administration').GetName]s, or cutting [Concept('concept_government_wage','$concept_government_wages$')].\n\nA less reliable but better way to improve your revenues is to grow your [concept_gdp] by improving the efficiency of your [Concept('concept_building', '$concept_buildings$')], or even deficit spending to expand profitable [Concept('concept_building', '$concept_buildings$')], though the latter can be tricky and is not a recommended course of action for new players.
lesson_budget_balance_how_1_desc: To reduce your deficit and pay off your loans you can either increase your revenues, cut your expenses, or both.
lesson_budget_balance_how_2_desc:
Your revenues consist of [concept_budget_minting] and [concept_taxes]. New currency will be minted automatically to keep pace with your growing economy, but [concept_taxes] are necessary to sustain powerful governments.

These can include:
 - [concept_budget_income_taxes]
 - [concept_budget_poll_taxes]
 - [Concept('concept_consumption_tax', '$concept_consumption_taxes$')]
 - [concept_budget_dividends_taxes]
 - [concept_tariffs]
and more.

Adding new or raising existing [concept_taxes] will increase your revenue immediately.
lesson_budget_balance_how_2_continue: Increase any Tax level or add a new [concept_consumption_tax] to continue
lesson_budget_balance_how_2_back: Close the Budget panel to backtrack
lesson_budget_balance_how_3_desc: Construction expenses are not considered part of your fixed expenses as they end as construction ends. They will still burden your [concept_treasury] while construction is ongoing. Let’s pause them for now, and you can restart them once you have resolved this problem.
lesson_budget_balance_how_3_continue: Pause all construction to halt construction expenses in all [Concept('concept_state', '$concept_states$')]
lesson_budget_balance_how_4_desc: Fixed expenses are incurred by [Concept('concept_government_building', '$concept_government_buildings$')] such as [SelectLocalization(GetPlayer.IsValid,'lesson_budget_balance_how_4_desc_added','Government Administration')] and [SelectLocalization(GetPlayer.IsValid,'lesson_budget_balance_how_4_desc_added_2','Barracks')], and include both [Concept('concept_good', '$concept_goods$')] used and [concept_budget_wages] paid by them. You can control your expenses by adjusting the $concept_budget_wages$ paid across your [concept_country].\n\nIf you wish, you can decrease [concept_budget_government_wages] or [concept_budget_military_wages] now. Wage changes are always reversible, but note the consequences in the tooltip!
lesson_budget_balance_how_5_desc: Another method of controlling your expenses is to downsize [Concept('concept_government_building', '$concept_government_buildings$')] in specific [Concept('concept_state', '$concept_states$')], permanently reducing the cost of both [concept_budget_wages] paid and [Concept('concept_good', '$concept_goods$')] consumed but removing the benefit that [concept_building] level provides.
lesson_budget_balance_how_6_desc: The [Concept('concept_state', '$concept_states$')] tab groups all [concept_treasury] revenues and expenses by [concept_state] to make it easier to find suitable candidates for downsizing. By sorting and hovering the Expenses value you can quickly find out which [Concept('concept_building', '$concept_buildings$')] cost you the most.\n\nIf you wish, you can reduce your expenses by downsizing [Concept('concept_government_building', '$concept_government_buildings$')] now. This can only be reversed by expanding the building again, which takes [concept_money] and time.
lesson_budget_balance_how_7_desc: A potentially major contributor to your fixed expenses is the [concept_budget_interest] paid on your [concept_loans].
lesson_budget_balance_how_7_continue: Click the Assets tab to continue
lesson_budget_balance_how_8_desc: You can only reduce [concept_budget_interest] payments by paying off your [concept_principal]. For as long as your [concept_treasury] balance is negative your $concept_principal$ will increase, increasing your $concept_budget_interest$ payments as well. If your $concept_treasury$ balance is positive you will automatically reduce your $concept_principal$ and $concept_budget_interest$ payments.\n\nIf you are able to reduce your $concept_budget_interest_rate$ you can take much larger [concept_loans] before succumbing to this death spiral.
lesson_budget_balance_how_9_desc: If your balance remains negative, continue raising or adding more [concept_taxes] and/or downsizing [Concept('concept_government_building', '$concept_government_buildings$')] until your balance is positive.
lesson_budget_balance_why_1_desc: There are many different sources of income and expenses. The Budget panel shows you a full breakdown.
lesson_budget_balance_why_1_continue: Open the Overview tab on the Budget panel
lesson_budget_balance_why_2_desc: If expenses exceed revenues your [concept_gold_reserves] will drain away each week as a negative #v Weekly balance#!. Once the [concept_gold_reserves] are empty, your [concept_loans] will increase every week. Whether you should consider this a problem or not depends on where the money is going.
lesson_budget_balance_why_2_back: Close the Overview tab on the Budget panel to backtrack
lesson_budget_balance_why_3_desc: Most expenses are #v fixed#!. The exact size of a fixed expense can vary over time depending on the economic conditions, but will remain week after week until you take measures to reduce them.\n\nConstruction costs, and other #v temporary#! expenses, are in effect for a certain period of time and then #v terminate#!. If your balance is only negative due to temporary expenses you usually don’t have to worry, since you are growing your economy and construction expenses can be paused at any time.
lesson_budget_balance_why_4_desc: But if your [concept_treasury] has larger #v fixed#! expenses than sources of income (revenue) your finances are unsustainable. Even if you have [concept_gold_reserves] you will eventually have to take [concept_loans] from your domestic industries just to continue operating.
lesson_budget_balance_why_5_desc: You should not be afraid to take [concept_loans] to get ahead, especially since most @money! you spend goes back into your [Concept('concept_pop','$concept_pops_possessive$')] pockets anyway! Remember that every [concept_good] bought and every @money! of [concept_budget_wages] paid ends up enriching either a producer, consumer, or both. Spending money from the [concept_treasury] always raises average [concept_wealth], which increases demand for [concept_pop_needs], which is what makes your economic wheels turn.
lesson_budget_balance_why_5_k_desc: You should not be afraid to take [Concept('concept_loans', '$concept_loans$')] to get ahead, especially since most @money! you spend goes back into your [Concept('concept_pop','$concept_pops_possessive$')] pockets anyway!
lesson_budget_balance_why_5_k2_desc: Remember that every [concept_good] bought and every @money! of [concept_budget_wages] paid ends up enriching either a producer, consumer, or both. Spending money from the [concept_treasury] always raises average [concept_wealth], which increases demand for [concept_pop_needs], which is what makes your economic wheels turn.
lesson_budget_balance_why_5_back: Close the Assets tab to backtrack
lesson_budget_balance_why_6_desc_common: Your total [concept_credit] is the sum of all buildings' [concept_cash_reserves]. The larger and more successful industries you have, the more you can borrow.
lesson_budget_balance_why_6_desc:
$lesson_budget_balance_why_6_desc_common$ Your remaining $concept_credit$ is:

#variable [GetPlayer.GetMaxCredit|2*]#! ([concept_credit]) - #variable [GetPlayer.GetPrincipal|K]#! ([concept_principal]) = #variable [GetPlayer.GetRemainingCredit|2*]#! remaining [concept_credit]

Hover the $concept_credit$ value to see a breakdown of your industries' $concept_cash_reserves$.
lesson_budget_balance_why_6_encyclopedia: $lesson_budget_balance_why_6_desc_common$ Remaining [concept_credit] is calculated as follows:\n\n[concept_credit] - [concept_principal] = remaining [concept_credit].
lesson_budget_balance_why_7_desc: If your [concept_principal] reaches your [concept_credit] your country is considered to be in [concept_default] as it cannot make good on its debts. This halts all construction and will [Concept('concept_radical', '$concept_radicalize$')] the country's [Concept('concept_pop', '$concept_pops$')] with [concept_privately_owned] [Concept('concept_building','$concept_buildings$')], which can be disastrous for political stability.
lesson_budget_balance_why_8_desc: Every change you make to your economy will have wide-ranging, indirect effects, in both positive and negative ways.
lesson_budget_balance_why_9_desc: All [concept_taxes] are collected directly from [Concept('concept_pop', '$concept_pops$')], though different tax [Concept('concept_law', '$concept_laws$')] will impact their personal finances differently. Similarly, all expenses affect your economy and the people making a living from it. By a simple act like raising taxes or adjusting [concept_budget_government_wages] to cover your expenses, you are in effect redistributing [concept_wealth] between your $concept_pops$. Every action has consequences for attributes like [concept_pop_growth] and [concept_turmoil].
lesson_budget_balance_why_9_back: Close the Overview tab on the Budget panel to backtrack
lesson_budget_balance_complete_1_desc: You have managed to restore a positive [concept_treasury] balance using a combination of the tools at your disposal. As your country progresses through the 19th century and beyond, you will be required to tweak your budget continuously to achieve stable growth without falling behind, or to recover from particularly costly events. The #b Budget#! panel will always display your income streams and expense outflows and help you optimize both.
lesson_budget_balance_fail_1_desc: The worst has come to pass - your [concept_treasury] is empty and you are now in [concept_default]. But do not worry, even this is something you can bounce back from. Keep trying to restore your balance and climb out of the whole, and if your [concept_budget_interest] payments are just too much to manage, you can declare [concept_bankruptcy] on the #b Asset#! tab in the #b Budget#! panel to seize your [Concept('concept_pop','$concept_pops_possessive$')] assets and rebuild your economy from scratch.
lesson_production_methods_how_1_desc: [Concept('concept_production_method', '$concept_production_methods$')] can be changed from the [concept_building] details panel. We will continue to use your [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetName] in [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetState.GetName] as an example.
lesson_production_methods_how_1_continue: Open the panel for the [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetName] in [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetState.GetName]
lesson_production_methods_how_2_desc: These are the [Concept('concept_production_method', '$concept_production_methods$')] currently in effect in this [concept_building]. You can click any of them to see a list of alternative options. The #g green#! number indicates the number of alternatives you have right now.
lesson_production_methods_how_2_back: [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetName] panel must be closed to backtrack
lesson_production_methods_how_3_desc: Hover any of the options for a breakdown of how the [concept_building] will change if that [concept_production_method] was selected instead.
lesson_production_methods_how_4_desc: Good job! You can see the new effects on the [concept_building] immediately, but repercussions on the [concept_workforce] and across the economy might take some time to materialize. Keep this [concept_production_method] active for at least [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTotalGoalValue|0] weeks to complete the lesson.
lesson_production_methods_why_1_desc: [Concept('concept_production_method', '$concept_production_methods$')] determine and change the functions of [Concept('concept_building','$concept_buildings$')]. For an example of this, we will look at the [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetName] in [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetState.GetName].
lesson_production_methods_why_1_continue: Open the panel for the [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetName] in [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetState.GetName]
lesson_production_methods_why_2_desc: If you hover over any of the active [Concept('concept_production_method', '$concept_production_methods$')] you can see in the tooltip how many [Concept('concept_good', '$concept_goods$')] that $concept_production_method$ consumes and produces. You can also see how many of each [concept_profession] it needs in the [concept_workforce] for the [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetName] to operate.
lesson_production_methods_why_3_desc:
[Concept('concept_production_method', '$concept_production_methods$')] are color-coded in different types:

#b Base#! $concept_production_methods$ use a productive [concept_workforce] made up of [Concept('concept_pop','$concept_pops$')] of different [Concept('concept_profession', '$concept_professions$')] to create a product or effect, often consuming one or several [Concept('concept_good', '$concept_goods$')] in the process. There is always at least one base type.

#b Refining#! $concept_production_methods$ reduce the amount of base $concept_goods$ produced to create more advanced or luxurious $concept_goods$, often by adding other input $concept_goods$ to the process.

#b Automation#! $concept_production_methods$ consume industrial $concept_goods$ but relieves the $concept_building$ from employing a lot of unskilled $concept_workforce$.

#b Ownership#! $concept_production_methods$ determine who owns the $concept_building$ and collects its [concept_dividends]. Which are available is usually determined by [Concept('concept_law', '$concept_laws$')].
lesson_production_methods_why_4_desc: If you click on any of the active [Concept('concept_production_method', '$concept_production_methods$')], you can see that each type includes different $concept_production_methods$, but only one can be active at a time. Some can be considered upgraded versions of previous ones in their type. These often require new [Concept('concept_technology', '$concept_technologies$')] to unlock. Others are simply alternatives, not inherently better or worse than the others. You have to decide what is best for your [concept_country] based on what [Concept('concept_good', '$concept_goods$')] and [Concept('concept_profession', '$concept_professions$')] you have and want.
lesson_production_methods_why_5_desc: Sometimes upgrading to a more modern [concept_production_method] is not desirable, particularly if the [concept_market_price] of its input [Concept('concept_good', '$concept_goods$')] are very expensive or even in a [Concept('concept_shortage','$concept_input_goods_shortage$')]. Another reason to not modernize right away is because the $concept_production_method$ require [Concept('concept_profession', '$concept_professions$')] which your [Concept('concept_pop', '$concept_pops$')] have poor [concept_pop_qualifications] for. You might even want to postpone upgrades because the new $concept_professions$ might be prone to political allegiances you are not comfortable with.
lesson_fix_unproductive_building_how_1_d: There is no one-click fix for a [Concept('concept_building', '$concept_building_possessive$')] low [concept_productivity]! Let’s have a look at the $concept_building$'s Process breakdown to see what the issues might be.
lesson_fix_unproductive_building_how_1_c: Open the $concept_state$ tab of [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetState.GetName] by clicking on the map. In the $concept_state$ $concept_building$ Tab, select the [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetName] $concept_building$
lesson_fix_unproductive_building_how_2_b: [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetName] panel must be closed to backtrack
lesson_fix_unproductive_building_how_2_d: If the [Concept('concept_good', '$concept_goods$')] on the input side of the Process are too expensive, you can focus on reducing their price. This can be accomplished by expanding [Concept('concept_building', '$concept_buildings$')] that produce them, or importing those $concept_goods$ to your [concept_market].
lesson_fix_unproductive_building_how_3_d: If the [Concept('concept_good', '$concept_goods$')] on the output side of the Process are too cheap, you can focus on raising their price. This could be an opportunity to expand [Concept('concept_building', '$concept_buildings$')] that consume those $concept_goods$, export those $concept_goods$ to other [Concept('concept_market', '$concept_markets$')], or encourage your [Concept('concept_pop', '$concept_pops$')] to consume them instead of other $concept_goods$.
lesson_fix_unproductive_building_how_4_d: If you want to engage in [concept_trade] to make the [Concept('concept_good', '$concept_goods$')] more profitable, you can do so by constructing a [GetBuildingType('building_trade_center').GetName] which can $concept_import$ or $concept_export$ $concept_goods$ autonomously via the [concept_world_market].
lesson_fix_unproductive_building_how_4_c: Stay on/Go back to the $concept_building$ details panel for the [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetName] in [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetState.GetName]
lesson_fix_unproductive_building_how_5_d: A different combination of [Concept('concept_production_method', '$concept_production_methods$')] might make the [concept_building] more [Concept('concept_productivity', '$concept_productive$')]. More modern $concept_production_methods$ are not always better, especially if their input [Concept('concept_good', '$concept_goods$')] are more costly! The impact of a $concept_production_method$ on a $concept_building$'s balance is displayed in its tooltip, so you can experiment with different methods to see if one works better.
lesson_fix_unproductive_building_how_6_d: [Concept('concept_decree', '$concept_decrees$')] can help increase the [concept_throughput] of a certain class of [Concept('concept_building', '$concept_buildings$')]. It is often not a good idea to increase the $concept_throughput$ of the [Concept('concept_productivity', '$concept_unproductive$')] $concept_building$ itself, since this could mean even more expensive input [Concept('concept_good', '$concept_goods$')] and even cheaper outputs.\n\nInstead, increase the $concept_throughput$ of $concept_buildings$ producing the input $concept_goods$' the $concept_building$ needs, or those which consume its output $concept_goods$. Finding ways for your $concept_buildings$ to benefit from each other is key to building a strong economy.
lesson_fix_unproductive_building_how_7_d: If there’s no good way to make a [concept_building] more [Concept('concept_productivity', '$concept_productive$')], but your economy still needs what the $concept_building$ produces, you can [Concept('concept_subsidies', '$concept_subsidize$')] it. This ensures it always has all the funds required to purchase its input [Concept('concept_good', '$concept_goods$')] and maintain a competitive [concept_building_wage] by covering any budgetary shortfalls from the [concept_treasury]. Your economic system law decides which $concept_buildings$ you may $concept_subsidize$.
lesson_fix_unproductive_building_how_8_d: [Concept('concept_building', '$concept_buildings$')] whose [concept_productivity] falls low enough that they can’t offer a competitive [concept_building_wage] will naturally adjust to the [concept_market], as their [concept_throughput] will be affected by lower employment which increases the earnings per remaining employee. If you want to speed up this process you can always downsize the $concept_building$ to force the workforce to go elsewhere. Note that this will anger the [Concept('concept_pop', '$concept_pops$')] that lose their jobs.
lesson_fix_unproductive_building_how_9_d: Use whatever tools at your disposal to improve the [concept_productivity] of this [concept_building]. If all else fails, you can [Concept('concept_subsidies', '$concept_subsidize$')] or even downsize it.
lesson_fix_unproductive_building_complet: The [concept_productivity] of the [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetName] in [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetBuilding.GetState.GetName] has recovered, paving the way for either increased [Concept('concept_building_wage', '$concept_building_wages$')], [concept_dividends], or both! Of course, you could always capitalize on the increase by raising [concept_taxes] instead, before the [concept_workforce] gets used to the financial improvements...\n\nBy checking up on your $concept_buildings$' $concept_productivity$ from time to time to make adjustments, you can ensure you have a good mix of $concept_buildings$ and that you’re not missing out on opportunities.
lesson_promote_movement_how_0_desc: Your country has no $country_bolster_ig_attraction_mult$ and therefore does not let you [concept_bolster] [Concept('concept_political_movement', '$concept_political_movements$')]. You must pass a [concept_law] that grants it first.[ConcatIfNeitherEmpty('\n\n',GetPlayer.GetModifier.GetDescFor('country_bolster_ig_attraction_mult'))]
lesson_promote_movement_how_0_continue: Open the Politics panel, click the Laws tab, and click the [GetPlayer.GetActiveLawFromGroup('lawgroup_free_speech').GetName] [concept_law] to see your possible options. Restart this lesson once your new $concept_law$ has been enacted!
lesson_promote_movement_how_1_desc: To [concept_bolster] a [concept_political_movement] you must first of all have a [concept_law] that permits it. This is defined mostly by your stance on [GetLawGroup('lawgroup_free_speech').GetName] (currently [GetPlayer.GetActiveLawFromGroup('lawgroup_free_speech').GetName]). By enacting different $concept_laws$ you can grant yourself more or less power to impact this.
lesson_promote_movement_how_2_desc: You can find a list of your currently active [Concept('concept_political_movement', '$concept_political_movements$')] on the $politics$ panel.
lesson_promote_movement_how_2_continue: Open the #v Politics#! panel and the #v Overview#! tab
lesson_promote_movement_how_3_desc: All [Concept('concept_political_movement', '$concept_political_movements$')] can be [Concept('concept_bolster', '$concept_bolstered$')], though it may be risky to $concept_bolster$ a $concept_political_movement_short$ with high [concept_activism].
lesson_promote_movement_how_3_continue: Click on a [concept_political_movement] you think looks interesting
lesson_promote_movement_how_3_back: Close the #v Politics#! panel and the #v Overview#! tab to backtrack
lesson_promote_movement_how_4_desc: [Concept('concept_bolster', '$concept_bolstering$')] [concept_political_movement] costs [concept_authority], and at the moment you do not have enough to spare. Review your $concept_authority$ expenditures and cancel enough of them that you have at least [GetDefine('NPolitics','BOLSTER_COST')|0v] @aut! $concept_authority$ available.
lesson_promote_movement_how_5_desc: You can choose to [concept_bolster] any [concept_political_movement], but remember, it comes at a cost of [concept_authority]. You $concept_bolster$ an $concept_political_movement$ by using the #b $concept_bolster$#! button the top of any $concept_political_movement$'s panel.
lesson_promote_movement_how_6_desc: A [Concept('concept_bolster', '$concept_bolstered$')] [concept_political_movement] does not radically change right away. Only the attraction changes, which will cause more eligible [Concept('concept_pop', '$concept_pops$')] to support it over time. Wait a while and you will soon see the impact on the $concept_political_movement$'s [concept_clout] and membership.
lesson_promote_movement_why_1_desc: [Concept('concept_political_movement', '$concept_political_movements$')] are instrumental in determining and shaping the politics of the [concept_interest_group] in your [concept_country].
lesson_promote_movement_why_2_desc: [Concept('concept_political_movement', '$concept_political_movements$')] will grow or wane in [concept_political_movement_support] over time. The $concept_political_movement_support$ grows and wanes along with changing conditions affecting [Concept('concept_pop', '$concept_pops$')] in your [concept_country]. This changing political landscape could come as a surprise to you and derail your plans.\n\nBy taking a more active role in deciding which $concept_political_movements$ to support you can both affect and more easily predict where your country is headed.
lesson_promote_movement_why_3_desc: A [Concept('concept_bolster', '$concept_bolstered$')] [concept_political_movement] will increase both its [concept_pop] membership and [concept_political_movement_support] over time. This will allow them to more easily influence the [Concept('concept_ideology', '$concept_ideologies$')] of your [Concept('concept_interest_group','$concept_interest_groups$')], which in turn can lead to an easier time enacting certain [Concept('concept_law', '$concept_laws$')].
lesson_promote_movement_why_4_desc: In addition to [Concept('concept_bolster', '$concept_bolstering$')] [Concept('concept_political_movement', '$concept_political_movements$')] you support, you can also [concept_suppress] those you oppose. Each of these actions cost a certain amount of @aut![Nbsp][concept_authority].
lesson_promote_movement_why_4_continue: Navigate to the [Concept('concept_law', '$concept_laws$')] tab on the $politics$ panel.
lesson_promote_movement_why_5_desc:
Your ability to [concept_bolster] and [concept_suppress] [Concept('concept_political_movement', '$concept_political_movements$')] is governed by two aspects:

* Your @aut![Nbsp][concept_authority] capacity
* Your values in $country_bolster_attraction_factor$ (currently [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetCountry.GetModifier.GetValueWithBreakdownFor('country_bolster_attraction_factor')]) and $country_suppression_attraction_factor$ (currently [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetCountry.GetModifier.GetValueWithBreakdownFor('country_suppression_attraction_factor')])

A prominent source for both of these is your current [concept_law] of [GetPlayer.GetActiveLawFromGroup('lawgroup_free_speech').GetName] under the [GetPlayer.GetActiveLawFromGroup('lawgroup_free_speech').GetGroup.GetName] [concept_law_group].
lesson_market_access_by_decree_how_0_des: This lesson requires you to be able to issue a [GetDecreeType('decree_road_maintenance').GetName] [concept_decree], but you currently have insufficient @aut![Nbsp][concept_authority] for that. Hovering @aut![Nbsp][concept_authority] in the top bar will produce a tooltip that explains why your balance is so low. Use this information to ensure your balance is at least #v [GetDecreeType('decree_road_maintenance').GetCost( GetPlayer.Self )|+=0]#! before restarting this lesson.
lesson_market_access_by_decree_how_0_con: You need at least [GetDecreeType('decree_road_maintenance').GetCost( GetPlayer.Self )] available @aut![Nbsp][concept_authority] to proceed. Skip this lesson and return once you do.
lesson_market_access_by_decree_how_1_des: You can easily increase the amount of [concept_infrastructure] available in a [concept_state] by issuing a [concept_decree] to maintain the roads there.
lesson_market_access_by_decree_how_1_con: Open the [concept_political_lens], then go to the $concept_decrees$ tab
lesson_market_access_by_decree_how_2_des: There are many different types of [Concept('concept_decree', '$concept_decrees$')] for you to issue. Decrees are always issued in a [concept_state] and cost [concept_authority] to maintain.
lesson_market_access_by_decree_how_2_con: Issue a Road Maintenance Decree in [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetState.GetName]
lesson_market_access_by_decree_how_2_bac: Close the $concept_decrees$ tab in the [concept_political_lens] to backtrack
lesson_market_access_by_decree_how_3_des: Great job! You have now issued a [GetDecreeType('decree_road_maintenance').GetName] [concept_decree] in [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetState.GetName] at a cost of @aut![Nbsp]#v [GetDecreeType('decree_road_maintenance').GetCost( GetPlayer.Self )|-0]#! [concept_authority].
lesson_market_access_by_decree_how_3_bac: Remove Road Maintenance Decree in [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetState.GetName] to backtrack
lesson_market_access_by_decree_how_4_des: You can see and manage your active [Concept('concept_decree', '$concept_decrees$')] in the $concept_political_lens$. They are also visible in the [concept_state] Panel Overview, and in this case the panel overview of [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetState.GetName].
lesson_market_access_by_decree_how_4_con: Click on the [concept_state] of [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetState.GetName] and go to the Overview tab
lesson_market_access_by_decree_how_5_des: The amount of [concept_infrastructure] and [concept_infrastructure_usage] is also visible on this panel. Hover the $concept_infrastructure$ value of [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetState.GetInfrastructure|v1] to see how much your [GetDecreeType('decree_road_maintenance').GetName] [concept_decree] adds.
lesson_market_access_by_decree_how_5_bac: Close the Overview tab of [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetState.GetName] to backtrack
lesson_market_access_by_decree_why_1_des:
[concept_market_access] represents how well-connected your [Concept('concept_state', '$concept_states$')] are to their [concept_market].

With #v 100%#! $concept_market_access$, a $concept_state$ will create 10 [concept_sell_orders] for every 10 [Concept('concept_good','$concept_goods$')] produced and 10 [concept_buy_orders] for every 10 $concept_goods$ consumed.

At #v 50%#! $concept_market_access$, the same amount of production or consumption would create only 5 $concept_buy_order_short$/$concept_sell_orders$ on the $concept_market$. This impacts the [concept_market_price] and drags your economy down.

Specializing your $concept_states$ while keeping them well-connected is key to running a prosperous nation.
lesson_market_access_by_decree_why_1_con: Open the Market panel to the Details tab for the [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetState.GetMarket.GetName]
lesson_market_access_by_decree_why_2_des: [concept_sell_orders] and [concept_buy_orders] determine a standard [concept_market_price] used across your [concept_market]. But with less than 100% [concept_market_access], [Concept('concept_state', '$concept_states$')] won’t be able to fully utilize the market. Some locally produced goods might drop in price, while goods whose demand cannot be met locally will increase in price, relative to the $concept_market_price$.
lesson_market_access_by_decree_why_2_bac: Close the Market panel to the Details tab for the [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetState.GetMarket.GetName] to backtrack
lesson_market_access_by_decree_why_3_des: Local price conditions can favor some [Concept('concept_pop', '$concept_pops$')] over others. In a [concept_state] with high [GetGoods('grain').GetTextIcon][Nbsp][GetGoods('grain').GetName] production but poor [concept_market_access], [GetGoods('grain').GetTextIcon][Nbsp][GetGoods('grain').GetName] will sell for a lower price than the [concept_market_price].\n\nWhile this might make the [concept_pop_needs] of the [concept_lower_strata] easier to meet, it will also limit the [Concept('concept_building_wage', '$concept_building_wages$')] that [GetGoods('grain').GetTextIcon][Nbsp][GetGoods('grain').GetName]-producing [Concept('concept_building', '$concept_buildings$')] can pay out. In the long run, $concept_states$ with poor [concept_market_access] will fall behind financially.
lesson_market_access_by_decree_why_4_des: [Concept('concept_decree', '$concept_decrees$')] can be used to impose an effect on a [concept_state] at the expense of @aut![Nbsp][concept_authority]. The effect will remain only for as long as the $concept_decree$ remains, so you need to choose carefully which $concept_decrees$ to use where since @aut![Nbsp]$concept_authority$ is a limited resource. Solving an [concept_infrastructure] shortage more permanently requires other approaches which you will learn about later.
lesson_market_access_with_railways_how_1: Railways can be constructed from the [concept_production_lens]
Open the $concept_production_lens$, then go to the $development_lens_tab$ tab
lesson_market_access_with_railways_how_2: Find Railways and build it in [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetState.GetName].
Close the $development_lens_tab$ tab in the $concept_production_lens$ to backtrack
lesson_market_access_with_railways_how_3: Great job! Construction is now in progress.\n\nRailways function like most other [Concept('concept_building', '$concept_buildings$')]. They take time and money to construct, after which they have to employ [Concept('concept_pop', '$concept_pops$')] to operate. They require [GetGoods('engines').GetTextIcon] [GetGoods('engines').GetName] and some kind of Fuel to operate, and provide [GetGoods('transportation').GetTextIcon] [GetGoods('transportation').GetName] for sale on the [concept_market].
Cancel construction building Railways in [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetState.GetName] to backtrack
lesson_market_access_with_railways_how_4: Both [Concept('concept_pop', '$concept_pops$')] and other [Concept('concept_building', '$concept_buildings$')] can purchase [GetGoods('transportation').GetTextIcon] [GetGoods('transportation').GetName], to fulfill [concept_pop_needs] or as part of a [concept_production_method]. But if demand is low and the cost of input goods is high, Railways can easily become unproductive and lose employees due to low [Concept('concept_building_wage', '$concept_building_wages$')]. To ensure optimal access to rail-based [concept_infrastructure] you may need to [Concept('concept_subsidies', '$concept_subsidize$')] Railways - either in specific [Concept('concept_state', '$concept_states$')] or all at once, if they are not already subsidized.
Open the $concept_buildings$ panel, click the Developments tab, and see if Railways are $concept_subsidized$
lesson_market_access_with_railways_how_5: It is possible that when construction completes and the Railway becomes fully employed, [concept_state] [concept_infrastructure] is still insufficient compared to [concept_infrastructure_usage]. If so, you can construct more Railways as long as you ensure they stay profitable, or subsidize them. At your option you could also downsize obsolete buildings contributing to the excessive $concept_infrastructure_usage$ in the $concept_state$.
Close the Developments tab in the $concept_buildings$ panel to backtrack
lesson_market_access_with_railways_why_1: [concept_infrastructure] is crucial to industrialization. Most [Concept('concept_building', '$concept_buildings$')] increase your [concept_infrastructure_usage], with heavier manufacturing industries adding the most. Having a [concept_market_access] below 100% is not always the end of the world, but it impacts both the [concept_local_price] and the [concept_market_price] of [Concept('concept_good', '$concept_goods$')] which will make industries uncompetitive in the long-term.
lesson_market_access_with_railways_why_2: You can easily address small [concept_infrastructure] shortages with the Road Maintenance Decree but this is a temporary solution at best, since [concept_authority] is hard for many countries to come by and you cannot use it everywhere in a larger country at once. Railways are always a superior alternative in the long-term, if you can afford the cost to build them and the labor (and potentially subsidies) required to operate them.
lesson_increase_immigration_how_1_desc: A [concept_state] will be an attractive target for [concept_migration] if the average [concept_sol] is high. [Concept('concept_pop', '$concept_pops$')] will move from States with lower [concept_migration_pull] to those with higher $concept_migration_pull$ in the same [concept_market].\n\nThere are several [concept_migration] map modes to activate in the map mode list next to the lenses which will give you an overview of where $concept_pops$ are $concept_migrating$. Feel free to check them out and continue whenever you are done.
lesson_increase_immigration_how_2_desc: Hover any [concept_state] to see its [concept_migration_pull] tooltip breakdown.\n\nWhen you are done looking at $concept_migration_pull$ tooltips, find [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetState.GetName] on the map.
lesson_increase_immigration_how_2_contin: Click [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetState.GetName] and open the Population tab
lesson_increase_immigration_how_2_back: Close the $concept_migration$ map mode to backtrack
lesson_increase_immigration_how_3_desc: A [Concept('concept_pop', '$concept_pop_possessive$')] [concept_sol] depends on many factors. The foremost among them are [concept_wealth], which in turn depends on how high their [Concept('concept_building_wage', '$concept_building_wages$')] are compared to the cost of their [concept_pop_needs].\n\nHover the average $concept_sol$ value for any of the stratas to see if they are above their [concept_expected_sol] or not.
lesson_increase_immigration_how_3_back: Close the Population tab for [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetState.GetName] to backtrack
lesson_increase_immigration_how_4_desc: If a [Concept('concept_state', '$concept_state_possessive$')] natural [concept_migration_pull] is insufficient you can increase it artificially by issuing a $decree_greener_grass_campaign$ $concept_decree$.
lesson_increase_immigration_how_5_desc: You can see how large of an effect the $decree_greener_grass_campaign$ has on [concept_migration_pull] and the projected migration to/from the [concept_state] in the Migration Attraction tooltip.
lesson_increase_immigration_why_1_desc: The most common reason to encourage [concept_migration] to a certain [concept_state] is to increase its labor supply to more effectively exploit its resources. Migration occurs naturally as poorer [Concept('concept_pop', '$concept_pops$')] seek better places to live and work in the same [concept_market]. Interfering in this process using [Concept('concept_law', '$concept_laws$')] or [Concept('concept_decree', '$concept_decrees$')] can speed up, slow down, or even reverse migration.
lesson_increase_immigration_why_1_contin: Open the [Concept('concept_culture', '$concept_cultures$')] tab in the Society Panel
lesson_increase_immigration_why_2_desc: High [concept_migration_pull] will not only make a [concept_state] a more attractive destination for [Concept('concept_pop', '$concept_pops$')] in the same [concept_market] and/or [concept_country], but will also increase the chance of it being randomly selected as a [concept_migration_target] for the mass movement of $concept_pops$ of [Concept('concept_culture', '$concept_cultures$')] with high average [concept_turmoil]. Hover a $concept_turmoil$ value to see both the global and national $concept_turmoil$ of that $concept_culture$.
lesson_increase_immigration_why_3_desc: To see if a specific [concept_culture] has any [Concept('concept_migration_target', '$concept_migration_targets$')], we can go in and look at that specific $concept_culture$.
lesson_increase_immigration_why_4_desc: A [Concept('concept_culture', '$concept_culture_possessive$')] [concept_migration_target] acts as a bridge permitting [Concept('concept_pop', '$concept_pops$')] of that $concept_culture$ to move there regardless of what [concept_market] they are in. $concept_pops$ will not move abroad unless they have a good reason to do so. If a $concept_pop$'s $concept_culture$ has no current $concept_migration_targets$, their [concept_migration] options are limited to States within the same $concept_market$.
lesson_increase_immigration_why_5_desc: Being selected as a [concept_migration_target] can have strong effects on your economy. These effects can be both beneficial and detrimental, as labor supply, [Concept('concept_good', '$concept_goods$')] demand, and [concept_turmoil] will all increase.
lesson_grow_gdp_how_1_desc: The easiest way to increase your [concept_gdp] is to spend money from the [concept_treasury] or [concept_investment_pool] to expand your productive buildings, or fix the ones that are unproductive.
lesson_grow_gdp_how_2_desc: As your economy optimizes, more [concept_wealth] is created which over time leads to greater [concept_pop] [concept_good_consumption]. If the increased demand for [Concept('concept_good','$concept_goods$')] can be fulfilled by local [concept_good_production], those buildings will become even more productive. If the demand can be satisfied only by [concept_trade], $concept_pops$ who work in the [GetBuildingType('building_trade_center').GetName] and those producing it in the exporting market benefit from it.
lesson_grow_gdp_how_3_desc: The fastest way to develop your [concept_gdp] is usually to manufacture consumer [Concept('concept_good', '$concept_goods$')] in high demand from basic resources. If you don't have access to all of those resources yourself, you can import them from a market that does. This does mean that your [concept_trade] partner will benefit from your economy, which also becomes more vulnerable to disruptions by hostile diplomacy or wars, so choose who you're trading with carefully!
lesson_grow_gdp_why_1_desc: Your [concept_gdp] is a useful way of measuring how powerful your economy is compared to others. Increasing $concept_gdp$ means that your [Concept('concept_pop','$concept_population$')] now spend their time on more productive pursuits, which increases [concept_wealth] in your country overall. This in turn increases both goods demand and [concept_sol], which creates more economic opportunities and population growth.
lesson_grow_gdp_why_2_desc:
[concept_gdp] isn't only a metric but does impact a number of other factors.

* It generates [concept_prestige]
* It lets you do more [concept_budget_minting]
* In a [concept_customs_union], it determines your [concept_market_share].
lesson_grow_gdp_complete_desc: You have proved yourself capable of growing your country's economy. As we go deeper into other aspects like politics and diplomacy, don't forget to continually expand in strategic directions so you don't get left behind! Growing your [concept_gdp] will not only increase your [concept_wealth], [concept_sol] and [concept_pop_growth] but also your [concept_prestige], which influences your [concept_rank], [concept_interest], and ability to engage in diplomacy.
lesson_enact_institution_law_how_1_desc: You can see which [Concept('concept_law','$concept_laws$')] you can enact, your success chances, and their effects on each specific [concept_law_group] panel. You find them under the #b $concept_laws$#! tab of the #b Politics#! Panel.
lesson_enact_institution_law_how_1_conti: Click the [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetLawType.GetGroup.GetName] $concept_law_group$ under the $concept_laws$ tab on the Politics Panel
lesson_enact_institution_law_how_2_desc: Your current [concept_law] in the [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetLawType.GetGroup.GetName] category is [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetLawType.GetName]. This $concept_law$ disables the [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetLawType.GetGroup.GetFirstInstitutionType.GetName] [concept_institution], so we have to enact an alternative to get access to it.\n\nAny of the other $concept_laws$ in the category will give us the $concept_institution$ we want, but different $concept_laws$ have different effects both on your [concept_country] and the $concept_institution$. If you have more options than one, inspect the effects before you decide which to enact.
lesson_enact_institution_law_how_3_desc: To even attempt to enact a [concept_law], it must have support by at least one government [concept_interest_group] or a currently active [concept_political_movement].\n\nThe capacity of your current [concept_government] to enact the $concept_law$ is measured by the chance that the $concept_law$ will pass, your so-called [concept_enactment_success] chance. Should you fail to pass the $concept_law$ on the first attempt, some other event will transpire and the outcome of that might increase or decrease your chances of success the next time around. The duration between attempts is determined by your [concept_legitimacy].
lesson_enact_institution_law_how_4_desc: Choose another [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetLawType.GetGroup.GetName] [concept_law] and start to enact it.\n\n@information! If you can not enact any $concept_law$, you need to put an [concept_interest_group] that [Concept('concept_endorse_oppose','$concept_endorse$')] any of the $concept_laws$ [concept_in_government].
lesson_enact_institution_law_how_4_conti: Start to enact anything else than [GetTutorialJournalEntry.GetTarget.GetLawType.GetName]
lesson_enact_institution_law_how_5_desc: [Concept('concept_law','$concept_laws$')] are not [Concept('concept_enactment_of_laws','$concept_enactment_of_laws_enacted$')] instantly. They will need to go through cycles where you may need to intervene to increase the [concept_enactment_success] chance of the law passing.
lesson_enact_institution_law_how_5_back: Cancel enactment of law to backtrack
lesson_enact_institution_law_why_1_desc: You can see which [Concept('concept_law','$concept_laws$')] you can enact, your success chances, and their effects on the #b $concept_laws$#! tab of the #b Politics#! Panel.
lesson_enact_institution_law_why_1_conti: Open the $concept_laws$ tab on the Politics Panel
lesson_enact_institution_law_why_2_desc: [Concept('concept_law','$concept_laws$')] determine your [Concept('concept_country','$concept_country_possessive$')] fundamental operating principles, everything from who holds the power and how your bureaucracies are organized, to how it gains and spends its [concept_money], to what rights the different segments of the [Concept('concept_pop','$concept_population$')] enjoys. Transforming your $concept_laws$ to keep up with the times is a necessity both due to practical reasons and to dodge your $concept_population$ rising up against you.
lesson_enact_institution_law_why_2_back: Close the $concept_laws$ tab on the Politics Panel
lesson_enact_institution_law_why_3_desc: You can see your current [Concept('concept_institution','$concept_institutions$')] on the $concept_institution$ tab.
lesson_enact_institution_law_why_3_conti: Open the $concept_institutions$ tab on the Politics Panel
lesson_enact_institution_law_why_4_desc: [Concept('concept_institution','$concept_institutions$')] are used to provide benefits for your nation or additional powers for you. In the process they use @bur![Nbsp][concept_bureaucracy], translating into an expense for the [concept_treasury] in relation to the size of your [Concept('concept_incorporated_state', '$concept_incorporated$')] population. To create a new $concept_institution$ you must enact a [concept_law] that enables it.
lesson_enact_institution_law_why_5_desc: Be aware that enacting [Concept('concept_law','$concept_laws$')] with a lot of resistance among the populace can be both an arduous and hazardous process. Certain $concept_laws$ can take a lot of finesse and statecraft to get smoothly through the legislature.
lesson_enact_institution_law_complete_de: You have managed to reform the first of many [Concept('concept_law','$concept_laws$')] on your country's journey through the Victorian era! Over time you will learn which combinations of government [Concept('concept_interest_group','$concept_interest_groups$')], [concept_clout], [concept_legitimacy], and [Concept('concept_political_movement', '$concept_political_movements$')] provide you with the best opportunities to pass the $concept_laws$ you desire. Until then, don't be afraid to experiment!
lesson_reform_government_how_1_desc: You can view the current composition of your Government on the #b $concept_government_reform$#! tab of the #b Politics#! Panel.
lesson_reform_government_how_1_continue: Open the $concept_government_reform$ tab on the Politics Panel
lesson_reform_government_how_1_back: Government Tab must be closed to backtrack
lesson_reform_government_how_2_desc: To reform your government, press the Reform Government button.
lesson_reform_government_how_3_desc: Here you can experiment with different configurations as much as you like. No change will take place until you Confirm the new government. You can also Reset your changes to return to the starting configuration.
lesson_reform_government_how_4_desc: Here you see the factors determining your Legitimacy based on your current Laws, and how the current prospective government configuration affects it.
lesson_reform_government_how_5_desc: Excluding Interest Groups that used to be in power will cause Radicalism among their ranks. Reforming your government too often can cause major political instability.\n\nYour first reform right after a democratic election does not cause any Radicalism. Use this opportunity to build an efficient government for the rest of the mandate period.
lesson_reform_government_how_6_desc: Legitimacy only impacts how efficiently your government operates, not what it is able to accomplish. Unless there is a Political Movement lending its support to a Law, in order to be enacted it must have the support of at least one Interest Group in government. The Laws the new government is willing to enact are listed while composing it, so ensure you have both the right mix of Interest Groups and sufficient Legitimacy to last you through the upcoming period.
lesson_reform_government_how_7_desc: Interest Groups can be moved in and out of government. If the Interest Group is a member of a Party in a democratic electoral system, the entire Party must be either in or out of government.\n\nSee if you can Reform your Government to have more than #v 60#! [concept_legitimacy]. If not, come back later and try again.
